## Summary

Fixes enemy wall-corner wedging during PURSUING state (issue #1457).

**v9 — adds position blacklist to v8 minimal fix:**

### Fix 1: \`MOTION_MODE_FLOATING\` (engine-level, primary fix)

\`CharacterBody2D\` defaults to \`MOTION_MODE_GROUNDED\`. In grounded mode, Godot's
physics engine classifies wall corner vertices as "floors" in top-down games.
Once classified as a floor, \`move_and_slide()\` applies floor-riding logic that
physically glues the body to the corner vertex every frame.

Setting \`motion_mode = MOTION_MODE_FLOATING\` in \`_ready()\` disables floor detection
entirely, which is correct for a top-down game.

Documented Godot engine bug:
- [godotengine/godot#109926](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/109926) (unfixed in Godot 4.5)
- [Godot Forum confirmation](https://forum.godotengine.org/t/characterbody2d-stops-to-follow-navigationagentline-when-reaching-a-walls-bottom-corner/92872)

### Fix 2: Pursuing stuck detection (defense-in-depth)

Adds a 1.5s stuck timer specific to PURSUING state cover movement:
- If enemy doesn't move >20px for 1.5s while navigating to cover, discard blocked
  cover and find a new route
- After 2 consecutive stucks, escalate to flanking or combat
- Resets on state transition

### Fix 3: Position blacklist (v9 — breaks reroute loop)

Root cause of v8 failure: after rerouting from a stuck position, navigation may
route back through the same corridor, causing repeated stuck-reroute-stuck loops.

Adds a small array of previously-stuck positions (`_pursuing_stuck_pos_blacklist`):
- When stuck fires, check if `global_position` is within 40px of a previously-stuck position
- If yes: **escalate immediately** to FLANKING or COMBAT (break the loop)
- If no: record position and proceed with reroute
- Clears on `_transition_to_pursuing()` for fresh slate on each new engagement

### What changed in \`enemy.gd\`
- **+1 line**: \`motion_mode = MOTION_MODE_FLOATING\` in \`_ready()\`
- **+4 lines**: Variable/constant declarations for stuck detection + position blacklist
- **~22 lines**: Stuck detection + position blacklist logic in \`_process_pursuing_state\`
- **+1 line**: Reset stuck state + clear blacklist in \`_transition_to_pursuing\`
- **No changes** to \`_move_to_target_nav\`, \`_apply_wall_avoidance\`, or any other function

### Deep case study (9 sessions)

Full session-by-session investigation is in \`docs/case-studies/issue-1457/CASE_STUDY.md\`:
- **9 game sessions analyzed** with actual logs (all in `docs/case-studies/issue-1457/logs/`)
- Screenshots of each stuck scenario
- Root cause traced from physics-level (MOTION_MODE_GROUNDED gluing) to navigation-level (reroute loop)
- Session 9 analysis: "AI completely broken" report = GDScript parse error in user's binary (not a regression from this fix)
- MOTION_MODE_FLOATING velocity accumulation bug (Godot #101052) documented — cosmetic only, not an infinite-stuck issue

## Test plan
- [ ] Use CI-built binary from [Build Windows Portable EXE](https://github.com/Jhon-Crow/godot-topdown-MVP/actions/runs/23560771838) artifact
- [ ] Verify enemies navigate around wall corners without getting stuck
- [ ] Verify enemies that do get briefly stuck escalate to flanking/combat instead of looping
- [ ] Verify enemies still pursue player cover-to-cover normally
- [ ] Verify flanking and combat transitions work
- [ ] Verify no regression in other AI states (SEARCHING, RETREATING, etc.)
- [ ] CI checks pass ✅

## 🔍 Session 5 Analysis + Fix v5 — Root Cause Found

Thanks for the screenshot and continued testing! The image shows exactly what's happening: the navigation path (yellow lines) points correctly through the corner, but the physics body is pinned there and can't follow it.

### Why all previous fixes (v1–v4) didn't fully solve it

All four previous iterations were treating **symptoms** (stuck detection, cover blacklist, escape impulse). The **root cause** is a Godot engine configuration issue:

**`CharacterBody2D.motion_mode` was not set** — it defaults to `MOTION_MODE_GROUNDED`. In grounded mode, the physics engine can classify wall corner vertices as "floors" at the moment of collision. Once it does, `move_and_slide()` applies floor-riding logic that **re-glues the body to the corner vertex every single frame**. No impulse can overcome this because the constraint is reapplied after every `move_and_slide()` call.

This is documented in Godot issue [#109926](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/109926) (open, unfixed in Godot 4.0–4.5) and confirmed by multiple Godot community threads for top-down games.

**Your friction observation** was precisely correct — this is the physics engine creating artificial "friction" at corner vertices.

### Fix v5 (two changes)

**1. `motion_mode = MOTION_MODE_FLOATING`** — one line in `_ready()`. This is the **canonical fix for top-down games** per Godot documentation and community consensus. It disables floor/ceiling detection so walls are never misclassified as floors.

**2. 3-probe forward steering (Craig Reynolds steering behaviors)** — added to `_move_to_target_nav`. Probes forward-left (−30°), forward, and forward-right (+30°) on every movement frame. If a side probe detects a wall ahead while the center path is clear, the enemy steers toward the open side proactively — preventing the approach to the corner wedge zone in the first place.

All v1–v4 safety nets (stuck detection, cover blacklist, escalation, escape impulse, nav reset) remain as defense-in-depth.

…ion + nav-mode avoidance

Two complementary fixes for enemies getting stuck on wall corners during PURSUING:

1. PURSUING-specific fast stuck detection (PURSUING_STUCK_MAX_TIME = 1.5s):
   Added _pursuing_stuck_timer / _pursuing_stuck_last_pos tracking inside the
   cover-movement branch of _process_pursuing_state. When the enemy has not moved
   more than PURSUING_STUCK_DIST_THRESHOLD (20px) for 1.5 s while heading toward
   pursuit cover, it immediately forces a cover re-search or falls back to
   flanking / combat. This is 2.7× faster than the global 4 s fallback and fires
   before the enemy is killed while visibly pinned.

2. Reduced wall avoidance weight in _move_to_target_nav (_apply_wall_avoidance_nav_mode):
   NavigationAgent2D already guarantees path is ≥ agent_radius (24px) from walls,
   so the standard 60px wall check was over-steering in corridors, causing
   oscillation that rubbed the enemy against adjacent walls. The new nav-mode
   variant uses 0.5× the normal weight (max ~0.35 instead of ~0.7), letting the
   computed nav path dominate while still providing escape force for direct collisions
   (Issue #1107 logic is unchanged).

Fixes Jhon-Crow/godot-topdown-MVP#1457

commits.messageBody:
Root-cause fix for enemy corner-wedging in PURSUING state.

**Root cause (confirmed):** CharacterBody2D defaults to MOTION_MODE_GROUNDED.
In a top-down game, this causes the physics engine to classify wall corners
as "floors" at the moment of collision (Godot issue #109926). Once classified
as a floor, move_and_slide applies floor-riding logic that glues the body to
the corner vertex — no impulse can overcome this per-frame constraint.

**Fix 1 — MOTION_MODE_FLOATING in _ready():**
Set `motion_mode = CharacterBody2D.MOTION_MODE_FLOATING` so the engine never
applies floor/ceiling logic. The body responds only to collision normals,
eliminating the physics corner-gluing entirely. This is the documented fix for
top-down and isometric games per Godot community and official docs.

**Fix 2 — 3-probe forward steering (Reynolds) in _move_to_target_nav:**
Probe forward-left (−30°), forward, and forward-right (+30°) each frame using
move_and_collide(test=true). If a side probe hits while center is clear, steer
0.6 weight toward the open side. If center is blocked, deflect 1.2 weight away
using the collision normal. This proactively routes the enemy around corners
before it gets close enough to wedge.

All v1–v4 safety nets retained (stuck detection, cover blacklist, escalation,
escape impulse, nav reset, separation skip) as defense-in-depth.

Added 2 regression tests:
- test_enemy_uses_floating_motion_mode_issue_1457: verifies MOTION_MODE_FLOATING
- test_three_probe_steering_exists_issue_1457: verifies ±0.524 rad probe angles

Evidence: 5 game logs analyzed across sessions 1–5. Root cause traced to
Godot engine #109926 (open, unfixed as of Godot 4.5 beta6). MOTION_MODE_FLOATING
is the canonical workaround per Godot forum (multiple confirmed threads 2024–2025).

Fixes Jhon-Crow/godot-topdown-MVP#1457
